---
title: "How do I calculate an interval for an observed yes/no proportion?"
---

## Question

How do I calculate an interval for an observed yes/no proportion?

## Decide which method fits

Define what counts as success; count successes and total eligible observations; choose the confidence level and inspect sampling assumptions.

## Worked example: mtcars

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("mtcars")
successes <- sum(d$am==1)
fit <- ru_apply("proportion_interval", successes=successes,
                n=nrow(d), confidence=.95)
stopifnot(is.finite(fit$estimate))
```

The calculation uses the proportion of cars marked as manual transmission among these recorded models. Because the sample is not established as representative, the interval is a mathematical illustration, not a justified estimate for all vehicles.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("proportion_interval", successes=your_success_count, n=your_sample_size, confidence=.95)
```

If the question asks only for the fraction in the observed dataset, divide successes by n and omit inference.

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("proportion_interval")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
